roadmap.goal: An eleventh usage data event, OptionalFeatureToggled (Epic #5733 vocabulary), sent when somebody switches a behaviour setting under Settings -> System and the server accepted the write. It carries which setting (optional_feature, from usage data's own closed list UsageDataOptionalFeature, which has one member: FeatureOrder) and which way (enabled, a JSON boolean). The veto (Never send usage data) is never reported in either direction, and a setting key the browser does not recognise sends nothing. The existing pipe does the rest: the browser notices, the backend checks consent and the veto, the backend forwards. Three steps. The backend goes first so that a browser never posts a name the server would refuse, because a refused message rejects the whole batch it travels in, and that batch carries other events. (1) Inbound: the server reads the event and refuses every other shape of it. (2) Outbound: the collector receives the two fields. (3) Frontend: the settings screen reports the switch after an accepted write. Done when: all 28 OptionalFeatureToggledEventTests cases are un-ignored and green; all 7 frontend cases in SystemSettingsTab.usageData.test.tsx and SystemSettingsTab.usageDataHandIn.test.tsx are un-skipped and green; `grep -rn "PendingDeliver\|it\.skip" ` over those three files returns zero matches; UsageDataDisclosureTest, UsageDataEmitSeamArchUnitTest and Slice04ProductEventsTests are green; `dotnet build` has zero warnings; the backend suite is green with `--filter "TestCategory!=Integration&TestCategory!=JiraIntegration&TestCategory!=LinearIntegration&TestCategory!=AdoIntegration&TestCategory!=ServiceNowIntegration"`; `pnpm test` and `pnpm build` are green with zero warnings. Mutation testing is a later gate that the maintainer approves separately. It runs after review, on frozen code, and is deliberately NOT a step here: Stryker.NET >= 80% on the changed lines of UsageDataEventShapes, UsageDataController's read and PostHogUsageDataPublisher, and StrykerJS >= 80% on the SystemSettingsTab handler and the key-to-name mapping. A warning for that gate: no unit test calls UsageDataEventShapes.Fits directly. The only thing that kills its mutants is the Integration/UsageData scenarios. If the Stryker.NET run excludes the acceptance suite, as this repository's Stryker config usually does, Fits will show survivors that the suite actually kills. Either include Integration/UsageData in that run or add a Fits unit spec at that gate.
roadmap.paradigm_note: The Hypothesis + state-delta unit mandate from nw-roadmap does not apply, and leaving it out is deliberate. This repository is C# + NUnit 4.6 + Moq on the backend and TypeScript + Vitest + React Testing Library on the frontend. There is no pytest-bdd, no .feature file and no Hypothesis. DISTILL recorded this in feature-delta.md under 'Completeness and mandate notes': layer-3 scenarios over real HTTP and SQLite, with the recorder below HttpClient. The input space is a one-member closed list plus a boolean, and B4-B8 enumerate it in full as [TestCase]/[TestCaseSource] rows, so a property generator would re-enumerate the same finite set. The 'exactly this changed, nothing else did' check is made through what the ports expose: the collector's message count, its exact outbound field set, and an empty collector. The crafter authors NO new acceptance tests. The 28 backend cases and 7 frontend cases were written by DISTILL and ship as [Ignore(PendingDeliver)] / it.skip. Each step's RED phase is removing those markers and watching the tests fail as red-classification.md recorded. Its GREEN phase is production code. Existing tests change only where DISTILL's Existing-test disposition table says so, each in the same commit as the production change that forces it, so no commit is red.

user_decisions: E1: one event, OptionalFeatureToggled = 10 on UsageDataEventName. The direction is a property, so both directions share one name.

E2: it carries exactly two things, optional_feature and enabled. Both are declared in UsageDataEventShapes both ways round: this event is refused without them, and every other event is refused with either of them. Never the setting's key string, name or description.

E3: the list of settings is usage data's own closed enum, UsageDataOptionalFeature, with one member, FeatureOrder = 0. It is not the product's key strings. DeltaSync is absent because story #5913 retired it.
E4: reported only after the server accepted the write. Never on the click, and never when the write is refused.

E5 (amended 2026-09-24, reversible): the veto (Never send usage data, key UsageData) is not reported in either direction. It is not on the enum, and the browser's key mapping leaves it out. The disclosure page says so.
E6: a setting key the browser does not recognise sends nothing. No guess and no placeholder.
E7: the disclosure page names the setting as the settings table does, *Let Lighthouse own the order of your Features*, using the default Terminology term.
out_of_scope: Any identity beyond the per-browser pseudonym: no instance id, no user, no customer (DISCUSS Out of Scope; ADR-191).
Reporting settings changes outside the behaviour-settings list, and reporting from the backend (API/MCP writes). The pipe is browser-detected by design.
Reporting the veto in either direction (E5). Making it reportable needs consent-refresh plumbing that this story does not build.
A PostHog insight or dashboard. Events are created on first arrival, so no DEVOPS change is needed (DESIGN: DEVOPS N/A).

Any change to Program.cs, the chart, the collector address, the consent gate, the veto gate, the daily allowance or the queue. Program.cs untouched also means CI does not force the full live-connector Integration suite.
Any EF migration. Nothing is persisted.
A separate unit spec for usageDataOptionalFeatureFor. DISTILL placed its coverage in F1-F5 through the call site. Add one at the Stryker gate only if a survivor asks for it.
A Playwright E2E. The flow is covered at the call site, the hand-in seam and the ingest endpoint, and E2E in this repository is a thin sanity layer.

Finalize-time items, not DELIVER steps: creating the ADO User Story (needs the maintainer's confirmation) and its Release Notes line; a kpi-contracts.yaml entry for OUT-usagedata-setting-switches if the maintainer wants one; ADO transitions (Resolved on push, Closed on CI green). phases.name: The server reads a behaviour-setting switch and forwards which setting and which way
phases.description: Inbound first, outbound second. 01-01 teaches the server to read OptionalFeatureToggled and to refuse every other shape of it: missing halves, settings not on the list, non-boolean directions, and the two fields on any other event. After that step the event is accepted, consent- and veto-gated, and forwarded under its name, but without its two fields, because the publisher does not know them yet. Nothing in the product sends it yet, so that intermediate state is unreachable. 01-02 teaches the publisher the two fields and widens the emit-seam field list by exactly those two names. The backend lands before the frontend on purpose: a browser posting a name the server cannot read gets its whole batch refused, and that loses every other event in the batch.

criteria: The RED run is captured BEFORE any production edit, with all 7 cases un-skipped, and it matches red-classification.md. F1: the 'not reported before the answer' leg passes, then the reporter is called 0 times where 1 was expected. F2-F5: the ordering control reported 0 times. F6: postEvents received nothing matching. Any import, type or setup failure is a finding to report.

Switching Feature Order reports nothing while the server has not answered. Once the write is accepted it reports exactly one OptionalFeatureToggled saying FeatureOrder and the new state (true). Switching it back reports one more with false (F1, F2).

Switching the veto (Never send usage data) reports nothing, whichever way it goes (F3). A switch the server refused reports nothing (F4). A setting whose key usage data has no name for reports nothing (F5). In each case the ordering switch that follows still reports once, so the silence is the rule and not a broken screen.
With the real consent answer, reporter and detector, the switch is handed to postEvents carrying name OptionalFeatureToggled, optionalFeature FeatureOrder and enabled true (F6).

The call site carries no consent branch. Whether anything is recorded stays the reporter's decision. SystemSettingsTab still renders where no consent provider is mounted: the existing SystemSettingsTab.test.tsx and SystemSettingsTab.behaviourSettings.test.tsx are green unedited.

No report is ever built with an optionalFeature the server would refuse: the mapping yields only FeatureOrder or nothing, and enabled is always a boolean. A refused message takes its whole batch down with it.
The TS mirrors use string values (the server answers and accepts names, not numbers). The key mapping is a Record, not a switch and not a pass-through of the stored key.
Comments give the reason in plain language and cite no internal reference ('E5', 'AC-1.3', 'U2').
`pnpm test` is green. `pnpm build` completes with zero errors and zero warnings, which implies a clean Biome check on ./src.
steps.implementation_notes:
Order: un-skip, capture RED with `pnpm vitest run src/pages/Settings/System/SystemSettingsTab.usageData.test.tsx src/pages/Settings/System/SystemSettingsTab.usageDataHandIn.test.tsx`, then production, then the full `pnpm test`, then `pnpm build`, then commit. The prebuild runs `biome check --write` and rewrites ./src, so build BEFORE staging and commit what the build left. Remove any `*/docs` symlink before building, or Biome reformats the docs tree. Frontend traps: take the reporter through useUsageDataReporter, which reads useUsageDataConsentIfKnown. Never call useUsageDataConsent from the screen: it throws outside UsageDataConsentProvider, and the screen's other tests mount none. Un-skip with it.skip -> it and it.skip.each -> it.each only. Never wrap in describe.skip: Vitest evaluates a skipped describe's body, so a hoisted scaffold call becomes a failed suite rather than pending tests. The direction reported is the new state, read from the row as it was before the click (`!toggledFeature.enabled`). The optimistic re-render hands the second click the updated row, which is what F2 relies on. Sonar/Biome: S7735 (no negated condition in a ternary); S7770 (pass single-arg functions directly); prefer globalThis over window if either is touched. No zod change: the server does not return these fields. Commit message:
feat(usage-data): report a behaviour setting switched once the server accepted it
